change.title: pr-8
change.description: FIX: proper handling of group memberships
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 pages for 50 members at limit 50 (and 3 for 100). With 50 members, `currentPage` is 1 and `totalPages` is 2, so `showingLast` is false and the "next" arrow stays enabled. Clicking it sets offset = min(50, 50) = 50 and loads an empty page labelled 2/2. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`. `currentPage` (line 8) has the same shape: an offset clamped to `user_count` shows a page past the end.

findings.title: Public group members page silently truncates to the first 50 members, with no paging UI
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` now defaults to `limit` 50 (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22) for every group. Before, non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups returned 200. The public `group-members` route (group-members.js.es6:8-11) calls `model.findMembers()` once and renders `members` here. The template has no next/previous controls and nothing calls `findMembers` with a different offset. A group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 with no sign that others exist. Either add pagination to this page, or keep the old limit on this endpoint and let only the admin UI request 50. The pending spec in spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb (lines 72-85) still parses the response as an array and will be wrong once un-pended, because the response is now `{members, meta}`.

findings.title: add_members raises a unique-index violation (500) when a username is already a member
findings.body: `group.add(user)` is `users.push(user)` (app/models/group.rb:272-274). `group_users` has a unique index on (group_id, user_id) (app/models/group_user.rb:18). The old `usernames=` path diffed against current members, so re-adding was harmless. The new endpoint pushes every listed user without checking. The client does not clear the input after Add (the `// TODO: should clear the input` in admin-group.js.es6:62), so clicking Add twice, or listing someone already in the group, re-sends the same usernames. This is likely to hit the unique index and return a 500 instead of ignoring the duplicate. Skip users already in `group.users`, or use `group.users.exists?(user.id)` / `unless`, before pushing.

findings.title: remove_member no longer clears the removed user's primary_group_id
findings.body: The previous membership-edit path (`usernames=` plus `destroy_deletions`, app/models/group.rb:287-295) nulled `users.primary_group_id` when it pointed at the group the user was removed from. `group.users.delete(user_id)` goes through the association and skips that hook, and nothing else in the controller does the cleanup. `primary_group_id` is only set from admin/users_controller.rb:135 and read by post_serializer.rb:97-100. A removed member can therefore keep a primary group they no longer belong to, so the group flair keeps showing on their posts. Clear it as `destroy_deletions` does: `User.where(id: user_id, primary_group_id: group.id).update_all(primary_group_id: nil)`.

findings.title: limit/offset from the client are not validated
findings.body: `params[:limit].to_i` and `params[:offset].to_i` go straight into `limit()`/`offset()`. A negative value (`?limit=-1`) should make Postgres reject the query and return a 500. An arbitrarily large limit returns the whole group, which defeats the paging this change adds. This is a public, unauthenticated-when-visible endpoint. Clamp `limit` to something like 1..200 and `offset` to >= 0.

findings.title: `usernames` on the singleton controller is never reset and leaks across groups
findings.body: `usernames: null` lives on the admin-group controller, which is reused as the user moves between groups. The route's `setupController` (admin_group_route.js:11-14) does not reset it. Text typed or selected for group A is still in the user-selector after switching to group B, and clicking Add then adds those users to B. The TODO on line 62 acknowledges that the input is not cleared after a successful add. Reset `usernames` in `setupController` and after a successful `addMembers`.

findings.title: Test coverage dropped for update and the new members endpoints
findings.body: The only `.update` test now covers an automatic group. The old coverage that a non-automatic group's name, alias_level and visible are updated is gone. The specs for `add_members` and `remove_member` do not cover non-existent usernames being ignored, re-adding an existing member, or the primary_group_id cleanup. The new `{members, meta}` response of `GroupsController#members` has no spec: the existing one in spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb is still pending and asserts the old array shape.

contracts.action: Admin group page loads and pages through members via group.findMembers() against /groups/:name/members.json
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously admin_group_route afterModel called findMembers and set `_members`; the public group-members route did the same.
contracts.before_after: Before: the route blocked on afterModel and set `members` or the model from the array result. Now: setupController sets the model and fires findMembers() without waiting, and the result is written onto the group (members, user_count, limit, offset) on resolve. The page renders with an empty list until the response arrives. The same group object is shared with the sidebar list, so user_count there updates too.
contracts.visible_effect: Admin sees a members list with N/M paging. Public page shows members from the same field but has no paging controls and is capped at 50.
contracts.failure_mode: findMembers() is not awaited and has no catch, so a rejected request only triggers the global ajax error handler. The list stays stale or empty. offset is clamped to user_count, which can leave a page past the end.

contracts.equivalent_path: Old `usernames=` + `destroy_deletions` path, and the old PATCH-delete via `group.remove`.
contracts.before_after: Before (usernames=): deleted group_users and nulled users.primary_group_id for those users in an after_save. Now: `group.users.delete(user_id)` then `group.save`, with no primary_group_id cleanup. The client then reloads the member list.
contracts.visible_effect: Member disappears from the list. A removed user keeps a stale primary_group_id.
contracts.failure_mode: Not-a-member ids are ignored silently. Automatic groups return 422, which the global ajax handler shows.

contracts.equivalent_path: Old `usernames=` replace-diff path, which only built group_users for names not already present.
contracts.before_after: Before: additions were computed as expected minus current, so duplicates were harmless. Now: every found user is pushed unconditionally, so an existing member hits the unique index on group_users.
contracts.visible_effect: The Add button reloads the list on success. The input is not cleared, so a second click re-sends the same names.
contracts.failure_mode: The unique-index violation should surface as a 500 and an ajax error popup. Nothing is added for users later in the list.

summary: The new member add/remove and paging code has four defects. `totalPages` is off by one when the member count is an exact multiple of the page size. The public group members page is now capped at 50 members with no paging UI. `add_members` can hit the unique index on group_users and return a 500 for an existing member. `remove_member` skips the `primary_group_id` cleanup the old path did. Two smaller points: the endpoint doesn't validate `limit` and `offset`, and the singleton `usernames` field leaks across groups. Test coverage also dropped for `update` and the new endpoints. I read every file in the part and did not run anything.
